meta.title: About — Israel Reis Pereira
meta.description: Meet Israel Reis Pereira, Information Systems student and developer in training, his projects, interests, and journey in technology.

hero.description: I am an Information Systems student and developer in training. I do not study technology just to know how to use tools. I build things to understand how they work.

whatYouGet.heading: Learn by building
whatYouGet.lead: My growth happens mainly when I turn knowledge into projects, test ideas, and document what I learn.

items.title: Practical building
items.description: I use projects to turn studied concepts into concrete development experiences.

items.title: Investigation
items.description: I try to understand how technologies work before simply adopting them.

items.title: Experimentation
items.description: I test different approaches to discover what works best in each context.

items.title: Documentation
items.description: I record decisions, problems, and lessons learned to make my evolution more organized.

items.title: Real projects
items.description: Each project is an opportunity to learn a technology, solve a problem, or consolidate a concept.

items.title: Long-term vision
items.description: I aim to build a technical foundation that remains useful as my career evolves.

items.title: Data and investigation
items.description: I am interested in understanding data, processes, and information as part of building systems.

items.title: Incremental evolution
items.description: I prefer improving systems in stages, learning from each version instead of trying to solve everything at once.

items.title: Infrastructure
items.description: I have a growing interest in infrastructure, automation, environments, and the processes that support applications.

principles.heading: Build with intention
principles.lead: Some principles guide the way I study technology and develop my projects.

items.title: Problem before technology
items.description: I try to understand the problem before choosing tools or architectures.

items.title: Incremental evolution
items.description: I prefer building a functional foundation and evolving the project as new problems and lessons emerge.

items.title: Objectivity
items.description: I seek simple, documented solutions that are coherent with the size and purpose of each project.

stack.title: My current foundation

faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.lead: A little more about my education, interests, and journey.

items.question: What are you studying?
items.answer: I am an Information Systems student at UniBarretos. I started the course in 2025 and have been using side projects to complement my academic education with practical experience.

items.question: Do you have a technical qualification?
items.answer: Yes. I completed the Technical Course in Systems Development at ETEC Coronel Raphael Brandão, which I attended between 2022 and 2024.

items.question: Why do you develop so many projects?
items.answer: Because I use projects as a laboratory. Building something forces me to research, make decisions, deal with errors, and better understand the concepts I study.

items.question: Which areas of technology interest you the most?
items.answer: I am mainly interested in software architecture, infrastructure, DevOps, SRE, data engineering, and application development.

items.question: What is your professional goal?
items.answer: To build a solid career in technology, developing a consistent technical foundation and seeking to create professional and financial value in the long term.

items.question: Which technologies do you use?
items.answer: The technologies present in my studies and projects include PHP, Node.js, JavaScript, C#/.NET, Blazor, Astro, MySQL, MariaDB, Git, and Docker.

items.question: Do you consider yourself an expert in these technologies?
items.answer: No. I am still in training, and I believe it is important to distinguish between knowledge gained through study, practical experience, and professional mastery. This website reflects that evolution.

items.question: Where can I follow your projects?
items.answer: The public projects, experiments, and studies that I choose to make available can be followed through my GitHub profile.

items.question: Do you work only with web development?
items.answer: Many of my current projects are related to web development, but my interests go beyond it and include architecture, infrastructure, data, automation, and software engineering.

items.question: Why do you document your projects?
items.answer: Because documentation helps understand decisions, record problems, and track a project's evolution. It also turns development into a more organized source of learning.

openSource.heading: Learning in public
openSource.description: Some of my studies and projects are developed openly, allowing others to follow decisions, experiments, problems, and evolution.

cards.title: Practical projects
cards.text: I use personal and academic projects as a laboratory to turn studied concepts into concrete applications.

cards.title: Continuous learning
cards.text: My education does not end with a specific technology. I am building a foundation that can keep pace with my professional growth.

cards.title: Documented evolution
cards.text: Whenever possible, I record decisions and development stages to understand not only the result, but also the path taken to reach it.

meta.title: Services — Web Development and Technology
meta.description: Web development, website creation, and digital solutions focused on organization, performance, maintenance, and continuous evolution.

hero.description: Projects developed with attention to the problem, code organization, and the possibility of future evolution.

design.heading: Web development
paragraphs: Web development means turning a need into an application that works clearly, is well organized, and is appropriate to its context.
I mainly work on web projects and use different technologies depending on the problem. The goal is not to use the newest tool, but to build a coherent, understandable solution that can evolve.

included.text: structured pages designed to present information clearly and make interaction easier.
projects organized to make understanding, maintenance, and evolution easier.
technical choices guided by the problem and the project's needs.
interfaces designed for different screen sizes and ways of accessing them.
a foundation that can receive improvements and new features as needs arise.

development.heading: Application development
paragraphs: I also develop applications for study and solving specific problems, using different technologies and architectures.
Projects such as PHP applications, C#/.NET systems, and Astro experiments are part of this process. Each has a different purpose and contributes to my development.

included.text: systems developed to solve specific problems through interfaces and application logic.
studies and projects using the .NET ecosystem and Blazor.
practical experience with PHP applications and databases such as MySQL and MariaDB.
development of modern websites using Astro, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS.
each application also serves as an environment to test concepts, tools, and architectural decisions.

performance.heading: Infrastructure and evolution
paragraphs: A system does not end when the code works. Environment, version control, documentation, security, and automation are also part of development.
I have a growing interest in this area and have been studying tools and practices related to infrastructure, DevOps, and SRE.

included.text: I use Git to track changes, organize versions, and record the evolution of projects.
recording decisions, configurations, pending issues, and processes to make projects easier to understand.
studies related to environments, hosting, servers, and how applications operate.
interest in automating repetitive processes and improving development reliability.
attention to basic security practices from the development and application configuration stages.

process.heading: How a project evolves
process.lead: From the initial problem to a functional and documented solution.

steps.title: Understanding
steps.description: First, I try to understand the problem, the project's goal, and the existing constraints.

steps.title: Planning
steps.description: I organize the requirements, technical decisions, and stages before starting implementation.

steps.title: Development
steps.description: I build the solution in smaller stages, testing and adjusting as the project evolves.

steps.title: Validation and documentation
steps.description: After implementation, I verify that everything works, record decisions, and identify what can be improved.

faq.heading: Questions and answers
faq.lead: Some information about my work and how I develop projects.

items.question: Do you develop websites?
items.answer: Yes. Web development is part of my current projects, especially using technologies such as Astro, TypeScript, and other tools from the web ecosystem.

items.question: Do you develop systems?
items.answer: Yes. I also develop applications and systems as part of my studies and projects, including work with PHP, C#/.NET, and databases.

items.question: Do you accept every project?
items.answer: No. Since I am still in training, I try to evaluate each project according to my technical ability, the problem involved, and the possibility of delivering something with quality.

items.question: Do you work alone?
items.answer: My personal projects and studies are developed individually, although that does not prevent collaboration when a project requires other people or knowledge.

items.question: Do you work on-site?
items.answer: Projects can be conducted remotely, using digital communication, version control, and documentation to organize the work.

items.question: Do you already master all these technologies?
items.answer: No. Some are part of more established practical experience, while others are still being studied. I prefer to present this transparently rather than treat every technology I study as professional mastery.

items.question: Why do you study so many technologies?
items.answer: I am not trying to accumulate tools. I use different technologies to understand different problems and build a broader development foundation.

items.question: Which area do you intend to pursue?
items.answer: I am interested in software development, architecture, infrastructure, DevOps/SRE, and data engineering. My journey is still being built.

items.question: Where do you intend to go professionally?
items.answer: I want to build a solid career in technology, develop a consistent technical foundation, and over time take on increasingly complex problems and responsibilities.

items.question: How can I follow your evolution?
items.answer: The best way is to follow my projects, public code, and the content I publish here on the website.
